Q3456346.decision: unresolved-equipment; retain existing record and no forced model assignment
findings: The naval action itself has plausible bibliographic leads, but no event-specific contemporary account was successfully inspected in this bounded review.

The apparent institutional corroboration in Puerto del Tomé: Antología Histórica, printed p.46, explicitly cites Spanish Wikipedia for this section. It is circular evidence and must not be promoted to an independent primary review.

That unverified lead describes Independencia as a steam tug and its opponent as an armed boat dispatched by Resolución. It does not establish a corvette, ironclad or powered Spanish gunboat. Do not depict the parent frigate as the captured launch.

Existing small-steam-gunboat requires screw propulsion/armed yacht evidence; paddle-steamer requires sidewheels. Neither is established here. Existing troop-transport model is a different function and dated 1904; do not extend merely to fill the gap.

Q126901559.decision: classification-review-hold-recommended; do not animate as opposing armies without further evidence
findings: The English article URL now redirects to Vega Expedition. This is a discovery warning, not the basis for exclusion.

Forum navale 67 pp. 19–20 places the first encounter in early September on the western peninsula, before wintering, and quotes a rifle discharge from Sven Andersson’s diary. It establishes neither organized Chukchi combatants nor a Swedish naval battle.

Nordenskiöld’s primary memoir vol. I p. 430 dates a first encounter off Cape Chelagskoj to 6 September 1878 and describes visitors including women and children. His account and the diary differ on the boats; do not assert they describe an identical instant or derive exact combat counts.

Memoir vol. I p. 8 says permission for the naval flag was refused; Vega sailed under the Swedish Yacht Club flag. The vessel description gives a barque rig and auxiliary engine. That does not justify a combat corvette.

Keep ethnic-group Q106991 unknown; no source supports promoting the entire people to military-unit. Existing inherited peninsula coordinate is not a verified encounter site. The 1878 year is compatible; this is a classification/model gap, not a demonstrated wrong year.
